description: hillmaker is a Python package that computes arrival, departure and occupancy profiles from transaction timestamps. The JOSS paper and own README name hospital emergency departments and surgical recovery rooms as capacity-planning examples. Spatial coverage is the facility or service network supplying records, and temporal coverage is the observed arrival and departure period. The repository reports MIT. Occupancy profiles can calibrate queueing or discrete-event simulations of hospital capacity under ordinary and surge conditions. A caveat is that timestamps may omit waiting before registration, blocked beds or transfers, and past arrivals may not represent a disaster surge. The tool summarizes events; it does not simulate care pathways itself. Patient data rights and privacy need separate handling. No directly related catalogue record was established. The article and own source were read without opening patient records or calculating a profile.
